title: DeepInfer zero-overhead scheduling: defer the previous step's post-process to overlap host prep with device work
summary: Move the CPU-only post-process of step N into step N+1 so it overlaps the next forward. The reusable part is the staleness enumeration and the on-device repair, not the scheduler itself.

hardware: Backend-independent pipelining idea; the reference implementation asserts support only for NVIDIA SM100 and Ascend 950
software: deepseek-ai/DeepInfer at 8b16149741a4935e1dec8cea27853f273b374c5b; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: Decode-heavy workload where the CPU post-process is exposed between device kernels
At least one extra step of retained metadata, state slots and KV blocks is affordable
Distributed step-type votes can run on a host-side backend, not a device collective
The entrypoint has a drain path, because callers see results one step late

claims.description: The reorder is forward(N) -> post-process(N-1) -> sample(N) -> defer post-process(N). Prompt steps never defer; only decode steps, and only when DEEPINFER_ZERO_OVERHEAD_SCHEDULING is set.

Three quantities become one step stale: per-request query length under adaptive speculation, per-request key length after rejected drafts, and input token ids for rows continuing from the previous batch. Each is repaired on device from a remap of the previous batch.

The scheduler releases the GIL; the standard ZOS engine constructor selects its CPU data-parallel group, created with Gloo, and the scheduler's Gloo vote uses a CPU tensor. This is a constructor/code path observation, not proof that every scheduler branch avoids device synchronization.

The default depends on how the engine object is built. The environment variable defaults false, while EngineArgs sets it with setdefault from a per-engine-type property that is true for NORMAL and COMPLETION and false for PROMPT. A README claim of 'enabled by default' and a false variable default can both be true of different entrypoints.

Forward and sample launches use a torch-visible synchronization debug guard. Event.synchronize is outside its coverage, another thread's allow scope can lift enforcement, and an environment setting disables it. Guard presence alone does not prove synchronization-free execution.

downstream_impact: The host-overhead profiling procedure measures exposed preparation; this source case illustrates moving that preparation rather than shrinking it, without a reproduced gain.
A vLLM or vLLM-family engine could adopt the reorder only if its scheduler is device-free and it can enumerate the stale quantities; neither is established here.
Ascend: the mechanism is arithmetic and metadata, but the reference asserts unsupported combinations rather than degrading, so the transfer hypothesis needs its own gate check.
recommendations: Treat the staleness list as the deliverable, not the code. An engine that cannot enumerate what becomes stale cannot safely pipeline.
Confirm the drain path before measuring anything; without it tokens are silently lost at the end of a request.
Preserve the standard ZOS constructor's host DP-group ordering, or re-establish the ordering for a custom construction before measuring overlap.
validation_plan: Profile with named regions before and after, reporting the idle window separately from kernel time.
Compare a fixed-seed single request token-for-token between the pipelined and direct orders.
Report the fraction of steps where the remap found overlap, split by prompt and decode.
Measure peak memory, since one extra step of state is retained.
limitations: No DeepInfer build or run was performed; nothing here is a measured gain.
The reference is an offline engine for one model; transfer to a serving engine with continuous batching is unproven.

Scheduler stale-output guards, sample-event synchronization and deferred metadata release exist. Their presence does not establish complete in-flight KV/state reuse safety; a reachable preemption race was neither proved nor reproduced, so it remains a validation question rather than a known defect.
Numeric timer thresholds and any reported throughput belong to the source deployment and are not reproduced.
